title: Farm to Fork
strapline: From the seed in the soil to the plate on the table — the whole journey of where our food really comes from.
intent: Children understand the journey of food — grown, harvested, prepared, cooked and eaten — as a connected story.
Children care for growing things and see the effort and time real food takes.
Children develop respect for food, farmers and the natural world that feeds us.
Children observe growth and change over time, from seed to harvest to meal.
Children build a willingness to try foods they have helped to grow and make.
implementation: Grow something edible — cress, beans, salad leaves, herbs — and care for it together over weeks.
Tell the whole story with pictures or a visit: seed, soil, sun, rain, growth, harvest, kitchen, plate.
Harvest what you've grown and prepare it into something simple to eat.
Talk about the farmers, the seasons and the weather that food depends on.
Set up a small-world or role-play farm-to-shop-to-kitchen so children replay the journey.
Keep a growing diary — photos, marks and measures — of the plant's progress.
Celebrate tasting the food you grew, and talk about where other foods on the plate begin.
key_questions: Where do you think this food started its journey?
What does our plant need to grow — and how can we help?
How long did it take from the seed to something we can eat?
Who grows the food that we don't grow ourselves?
Would you like to taste what we grew?

impact.text: Children understand the connected journey of food from seed to plate.
Children care for growing things and see the time and effort real food takes.
Children observe growth and change over time and talk about it.
Children talk about farmers, seasons and the weather that food depends on.
Children willingly try foods they have grown and helped prepare.
Children ask real questions about where food comes from and expect real answers.

enhancements: A growing patch or pots of cress, beans, herbs or salad.
A farm-to-fork picture sequence to order and retell.
A growing diary with photos, drawings and measurements.
Small-world farm, shop and kitchen for replaying the journey.
Watering cans, trowels and a harvest basket.
Simple recipes for cooking what you've grown.
A tasting table for the harvest, with foods to compare.

playing_exploring: Children get hands-in-the-soil, planting, watering and harvesting for real.
They replay the food journey in small-world and role play.
active_learning: Caring for a plant over weeks builds patience and responsibility.
Children see a long process through from seed to shared meal.
creating_thinking: Children make links across the whole journey — soil, sun, harvest, plate.
They ask and answer real questions about where their food begins.
